core_obligations: Setup and degree identity (proof lines 6042-6060): for reduced connected Y of dimension 1, k' = H^0(Y, O_Y) is a finite extension of k dividing all invariants; the restriction sequence against the complement Z gives deg(omega_X|_Y) = deg(Y cap Z) - 2 chi(Y, O_Y).

Failure analysis (proof lines 6061-6070): if the inequality failed then 2[k' : k] > deg(Y cap Z) + dim H^1(Y, O_Y), which by nonemptiness and divisibility forces Y cap Z to be a single k'-rational point of the smooth locus with H^1(Y, O_Y) = 0.

Conclusion (proof lines 6071-6077): irreducible Y is then a rational tail; reducible Y has deg(omega_X|_Y) = -[k' : k], so some component C has negative canonical degree by the degree-in-components lemma, and the same analysis on C exhibits a rational tail.
proof_roadmap: Fix the complement and derive the degree identity from the restriction sequence.
Under failure of the inequality, use divisibility to isolate the single-point smooth-locus configuration.
Conclude a rational tail directly when Y is irreducible.
In the reducible case drop to a negative-degree component and rerun the analysis.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the degree inequality powering the tail/bridge analysis of the chapter (statement lines 6032-6040). The proof (lines 6042-6077) is complete: the restriction-sequence degree identity over the field of definition, the divisibility-driven exclusion leaving the single rational point with vanishing H^1, and the two-case conclusion (irreducible gives a tail; reducible drops to a negative-degree component and repeats). Every step is present with no omissions. H2: the same systematic machinery as the companion ampleness lemma, correctly ordered.
